sections.label: Film licences and classification
sections.summary: Distributors and exhibitors must obtain an IMDA licence, and all films must be submitted to IMDA for classification.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Under the Act, distributors and exhibitors are required to obtain a licence from the Info-communications Media Development Authority of Singapore (IMDA).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: All films also need to be submitted to IMDA for classification.

sections.label: Singapore cinema attendance rates
sections.summary: Singapore moviegoers make over 20 million cinema visits annually, one of the world's highest per-capita attendance rates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Today, Singapore moviegoers clock more than 20 million visits annually, achieving one of the highest per-capita cinema attendance rates in the world.

sections.label: External film content assessors
sections.summary: The scheme lets IMDA-trained external content assessors classify films and videos up to PG13.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The scheme involves allowing external film content assessors (CAs) trained by IMDA to classify films and videos up to Parents Strongly Cautioned (PG13).

sections.label: Licence for film business
sections.summary: Section 6 clarifies a licence is required for distributing or publicly exhibiting films in any business, regardless of core business.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Second, section 6 will also clarify that a licence is required for the distribution or the public exhibition of films in the course of any business, regardless of whether the core business involves film distribution or exhibition.

sections.label: Class licences and video games
sections.summary: Section 10A lets IMDA create class licences, clause 3 defines video games as physical only, and an automatic class licence covers video game retailers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Fourth, section 10A is introduced to allow IMDA to create a system of class licences for film activities where a lighter regulatory approach is appropriate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Clause 3 introduces a new definition for video games, to clarify that only physical video games will be regulated under the amended Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: These changes will enable IMDA to enhance the protection of minors by establishing an automatic class licence for retailers of video games.

sections.label: FAC membership and quorum
sections.summary: Section 25 is amended to let the Minister appoint 15 to 21 FAC members, change quorum to one-third, and set terms up to three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Lastly, section 25 is amended to allow the Minister to appoint between 15 and 21 members to FAC instead of 15 members currently, to change the quorum from five members to at least one-third of members, and to determine the term of FAC members for up to three years.

sections.label: IMDA enforcement powers gaps
sections.summary: IMDA's existing enforcement powers do not cover serious offences such as Minister-prohibited films and unlicensed public exhibition.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: First, IMDA's existing enforcement powers do not cover several serious offences, such as those involving films prohibited by the Minister on public interest grounds and unlicensed public exhibition.

sections.label: New IMDA enforcement powers
sections.summary: New sections empower IMDA to request information, require attendance and search and seize, confined to prohibited films and unlicensed exhibition.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Sections 23, 34 and 34A in clauses 11 and 20 will address these gaps.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: These new sections empower IMDA to: first, request information and documents that are necessary to ensure compliance with the amended FA and gain access to places where films are publicly exhibited or distributed for inspection purposes; second, require the attendance of persons for the purpose of investigating breaches and offences under the amended FA; and third, enter with the occupier's consent or a Court warrant, search and seize evidence with a Court warrant for FA offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We have also made several adjustments to address public feedback.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We have confined these powers to the more serious offences, extending them only to those involving prohibited films and the unlicensed public exhibition of films.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In addition, all enforcement powers will only be exercised by IMDA's enforcement officers who are and will continue to be trained by the Home Team.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We have also provided an avenue so that owners can challenge seizures of their items in Court within 48 hours of the seizure.

sections.label: Composition and consequential amendments
sections.summary: Section 38B provides for composition of less serious offences, with consequential amendments to the Film Hire Duty and Public Entertainments Acts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Section 38B provides for the composition of less serious offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Consequential amendments are also made to the Cinematograph Film Hire Duty Act due to the transfer of functions from BFC to IMDA, and the Public Entertainments Act as it has cross-referenced the FA's definition of "film".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: MCI and IMDA will continue to review both local and international developments and consider future changes to the Act when the time is right.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The FA sets out the framework for regulating the distribution, exhibition and possession of films in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: MCI's amendments to the Act, following a wide review, aims to help develop our media industry in Singapore, without undermining our religious and racial harmony, public interest and matters of security.

sections.label: Co-Classification Scheme formalised
sections.summary: The new Films Bill formalises the Co-Classification Scheme, under which CAs co-classify prescribed films for PG13 and below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Starting with the new Films Bill which will formalise the Co-Classification Scheme, IMDA has piloted co-classification by film CAs for PG13 and below, and CAs can only co-classify prescribed categories of films for PG13 and below.

sections.label: IMDA takes over Police enforcement
sections.summary: Under the new Act, IMDA takes over enforcement authority from the Police, with officers granted powers to enter, search and seize evidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under the new Act, IMDA will undertake the enforcement authority from the Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As such, the IMDA enforcement officers will be granted powers to enter, search and seize evidential materials, such as film-making equipment, to enforce against FA offences.

sections.label: Safeguards for enforcement officers
sections.summary: Entry and search will be authorised by senior IMDA officers holding the title of Director or equivalent to ensure accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In particular, for new enforcement officers who may have very little or any relevant experience, what are the safeguards in place when they carry out the above activities?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We have to assure the public that the processes are in place to prevent abuse of authority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For, one, we need to ensure the accountability of the enforcement officers’ actions and that the enforcement powers are exercised judiciously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For instance, all entry and search will be authorised by senior IMDA officers holding the title of Director or equivalent.

sections.label: Filmmakers' position paper concerns
sections.summary: During consultation, 48 filmmakers, half of them well-known, put out a position paper raising their concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With that, during the consultation, the film community has put out a position paper whereby 48 filmmakers, and half of them well-known filmmakers, have raised their concerns.

sections.label: Proposed section 16 classification refusal
sections.summary: Proposed section 16 refuses classification to films against national security or containing prescribed material, and filmmakers fear unclear terms restrict production.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under the proposed section 16, a film that is, among others, "against national security" or that "contains any material prescribed", will be refused classification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Having spoken to some filmmakers, they have expressed concerns that the lack of clarity of the above terms may have the unintended effect of restricting and impeding how to produce their films, since they do not know whether the content of their films may have crossed the boundaries such that it becomes against national security and, therefore, refused a classification.

sections.label: Interventions in creative process
sections.summary: Interventions could occur from scripting to editing to fit lower age ratings, leaving filmmakers with less bargaining power and compromised artistic vision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With so many interests at stake, it could be a case whereby interventions can happen even at the creative process, as early as scripting stage, editing stage, to cut out more, in order to fit lower age-restriction ratings and, in this equal system, the filmmakers may find themselves in a disadvantageous position with lesser bargaining power and have to compromise their artistic vision.

sections.label: Proposed section 34 enforcement powers
sections.summary: Proposed section 34 with 34A gives enforcement officers powers to enter using reasonable force and seize films, advertisements or equipment without warrant on reasonable suspicion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under the proposed section 34 that is read with section 34A, enforcement officers are given overarching powers, such as being permitted to enter a place "using such force as is reasonably necessary to obtain entry", or to seize any film, advertisement or equipment that may be evidential material without warrant if the enforcement officers "reasonably suspect" that certain offences have been committed.

sections.label: Expanded search and seizure powers
sections.summary: Expanded powers let IMDA officers break in to collect evidential and non-evidential materials, including phones, tablets, laptops, computers and storage devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this Bill, the expanding search and seize powers allow for IMDA enforcement officers to break into any venue to collect any "evidential materials" as well as "not evidential materials" that they happen to take.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must be reminded that what they can seize are not just DVDs or film reels, but now also include personal digital devices, including mobile phones, personal tablets, laptops, computers and any type of storage devices, including thumbdrives, which will now be materials that can be seized for prosecution.

sections.label: Right to be heard legislated
sections.summary: FAC currently gives aggrieved appellants a right to be heard, but without legislation under the FA this practice is not guaranteed to continue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As I understand it, the current practice is that FAC does give an aggrieved individual who is appealing a decision of IMDA the right to be heard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, unless the right to be heard is legislated under the FA, there is simply no guarantee such a practice will continue.

sections.label: Film industry representation on committee
sections.summary: One of 15 committee members is from the film industry, and the speaker says more film industry members would benefit the committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Presently, only one out of the 15 members of the committee is from the film industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also note that the present committee comprises a few civil servants, school principals, professors as well as lawyers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, given that the Committee of Appeal will be dealing with appeal matters concerning appeals from filmmakers, I feel that having more members from the film industry will be beneficial to the committee, in terms of the relevant experience and expertise that members of the film industry can contribute.

sections.label: Grounds of appeal decision
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister whether applicants will be given the grounds of decision by the Committee of Appeal or the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I have one more clarification that I hope the Minister can address.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note that the proposed section 24 and 24A of the Bill is silent as to whether the applicant making the appeal will be provided the grounds of decision made by either the Committee of Appeal or the Minister.

sections.label: Private party political film liability
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a person who makes a party political film only for private viewing would be criminally liable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is clear from the above that private viewing of a film is not sought to be criminalised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, if a person makes a party political film for the sole purpose of viewing it by him or herself without any intention of publishing or distributing such a film, would such a person be criminally liable?

sections.label: Amending section 33(b) disparity
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to consider amending section 33(b) to address the disparity in standards for party and non-party political films.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It seems disproportionate that such an individual may be criminally liable for the making of such a video under section 33(b) of the present FA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I, therefore, hope that the Minister can consider also amending section 33 (b) of the present FA to address the disparity in the standards, where the making and reproduction of party political films are criminalised, but the making and reproduction of non-party political films are not criminalised under the new amendments.

sections.label: Art maker on classification and censorship
sections.summary: An art maker says classification and censorship differ, that censorship prevails, and that he is unsure he can support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Why should I, the maker of the artistic work, be the one doing regulatory monitoring and censorship for IMDA?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: So, in light of those concerns, I am, at the moment, not really sure if I can support this particular Bill because there is a difference between classification and censorship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: And in this case, I would not say that there is no censorship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: There is classification, but censorship do prevail and that is something that I, as an art maker, fundamentally feel is a problem.

sections.label: Expanded definition of exhibit
sections.summary: The Bill's expanded definition of exhibit means displaying, screening or projecting a film's contents so another individual may see it.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The expanded definition of "exhibit" in the Bill means "to display, screen or project the contents contained in the film in order that another individual may see it (regardless of the manner of the film’s reception)".

sections.label: Exhibiting films in public
sections.summary: Asks whether watching a film in a public place or sharing a video through Whatsapp or Facebook counts as exhibiting a film.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would someone watching a film on his or her laptop or mobile device in a public place, where it is inevitable others standing or sitting close by would also watch the film, be exhibiting a film?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would someone who shares a video recording with friends through Whatsapp or Facebook be exhibiting a film?

sections.label: IMDA licensing and classification balance
sections.summary: Asks the Minister to clarify how IMDA intends to achieve this balance in the new licensing and classification regime.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would the Minister clarify how IMDA intends to achieve this balance in the new licensing and classification regime?

sections.label: Party Political Film definition amended
sections.summary: The Party Political Film definition was amended in 2009 to allow greater responsible and reasonable discussion of politics, after first being regulated in 1998.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The definition of Party Political Film (PPF) was amended to allow for greater responsible and reasonable discussion of politics in 2009 after the PPF was first regulated in 1998.

sections.label: Warrantless search and seizure powers
sections.summary: IMDA officers' powers to enter, search and seize without warrant are now an exception under new section 34A, exercisable in two stated situations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The powers of IMDA officers to enter, search and seize without warrant are now made an exception in the new section 34A.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Officers can only exercise the exceptional powers to conduct search and seizure without warrant in two situations: the first situation is that they suspect, on reasonable grounds, that one of the more serious offences has been or is being committed; and the second situation is that they have a reasonable cause to believe that evidence of the offence can be found in the place and it is necessary to secure the evidence immediately.

sections.label: Challenging search and seizure
sections.summary: Asks whether the reasonable grounds of suspicion and reasonable cause of belief would be set out so affected persons could challenge the seizure in Court within 48 hours.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Second, would the Minister clarify if the reasonable grounds of suspicion of the commission of offence and the reasonable cause of belief that evidence can be found and need to be secured, would be set out to the person or persons affected by the search and seizure so that they could challenge the seizure in Court within 48 hours if they deem the seizure unreasonable?

sections.label: Regulating films gingerly
sections.summary: Expresses hope that IMDA would regulate films, especially those by budding local directors, extremely cautiously and also delicately and elegantly.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Today, "gingerly" means "extremely cautiously", but I also like the old meanings of "delicately and elegantly" that are not altogether lost in the word.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I hope IMDA would regulate films, especially films produced by our budding local directors, extremely cautiously and also delicately and elegantly.

sections.label: Appeals process for classification decisions
sections.summary: New sections 24 to 27 set out the appeals process for classification decisions, with a Committee of Appeal and the Minister as appellate authorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new sections 24 to 27 set out the appeals process for classification decisions, for which there are two appellate authorities – a Committee of Appeal and the Minister.

sections.label: Committee of Appeal and classification refusal
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes new section 25 increasing Committee of Appeal members, and notes section 16 lets IMDA refuse classification in five categories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, I do welcome the new section 25, which will increase the number of members sitting on the Committee of Appeal, which may provide for greater diversity of views.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, under section 16, IMDA may refuse to classify films in five stated categories.

sections.label: New co-classification scheme
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a new co-classification scheme, welcomed by distributors as it shortens classification processing time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill also introduces a new co-classification scheme, which has been welcomed by distributors as it shortens the processing time for classifications.

sections.label: Listing and advertising films with cuts
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Minister will require all films with cuts to be expressly listed and visibly advertised as such.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Minister consider requiring all films with cuts to be expressly listed and visibly advertised as such so that consumers are not shortchanged?

sections.label: Who are enforcement officers
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to clarify who will be classified as enforcement officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify who will be classified as enforcement officers?

sections.label: Guidelines for enforcement powers
sections.summary: The question asks whether guidelines for enforcement powers will be issued and made publicly available for public awareness of rights and recourse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will guidelines be issued for the exercise of their enforcement powers, and will they be publicly available so that members of the public are aware of their rights and available recourse should their personal devices be seized?

sections.label: Safeguards for seized device materials
sections.summary: The passage asks what safeguards ensure personal materials on seized devices will not be accessed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What safeguards are there to ensure that personal materials on the devices seized will not be accessed?

sections.label: Amendments after 1998 review
sections.summary: The passage states the last major review was in 1998 and amendments are warranted by technological and industry developments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The last major review was in 1998 and, in the last 20 years, there have been significant technological and industry developments that warrant amendments to keep the Act relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In particular, the amendments will help cater to the advancements brought about by the digital revolution, strengthen the protection of minors and, generally, make it easier for businesses to function.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As video games have become more sophisticated and include mature content on sex, violence and drugs, retailers should be taken to task if licensing conditions are breached.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This amendment will ensure that all retailers will have to comply with licensing conditions like labelling and age checks.

sections.label: IMDA test co-classification scheme
sections.summary: IMDA, then MDA, piloted a test co-classification scheme in 2011 and classified about 2,300 titles rated PG13 and below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: IMDA, or the Media Development Authority (MDA) as it was known then, also successfully piloted a test co-classification scheme in 2011 and classified some 2,300 titles rated PG13 and below.

sections.label: Committee representation and appeals
sections.summary: The passage suggests options for broad Committee representation, publishing members' names and bios, and the Minister hearing appeals for films with national security concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Perhaps a more practical approach would be for the Ministry to consider options that would ensure that the Committee reflects a broad representation of the average Singaporean film audience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This would ensure that any allegations or concerns about the dominance of particular lobby groups or a vocal minority can be addressed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And once these appointments are made, the Ministry should make public the names and the bios of all Committee members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Another issue that has prompted feedback is the amendment to make the Minister the final authority to hear appeals for films with national security concerns.

sections.label: Minister deciding national security film appeals
sections.summary: The passage states foreign influencers can target the creative community and the Minister is best placed to decide appeals on such films.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And with the digital disruption upon us, foreign influencers can also target the creative community through funding and other more sophisticated means.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe that the Minister would be best placed to decide on appeals concerning such films as he will have the entire machinery of the Government’s security agencies to examine the sensitivity of the issues involved.

sections.label: Registering film classification administrators
sections.summary: The passage states Section 19 of the Bill provides for individuals to be registered as film CAs to administer film classification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Section 19 of the Bill provides for individuals to be registered as film CAs to administer the classification of films.

sections.label: Committee size and term changes
sections.summary: Clause 12 amends section 25 so the committee comprises 15 to 21 members, appointed for terms not exceeding three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Clause 12 in the Bill amends section 25 to modify the composition of this committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is encouraging to note that the committee size is no longer fixed at 15 but is now stipulated to comprise between a minimum of 15 members and a maximum of 21, with an appointment period not exceeding a three-year term.

sections.label: Appeals on national security films
sections.summary: Clause 11 introduces a new section 24 for appeals to the Minister against decisions refusing to classify or reclassify a film on national security grounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Clause 11 introduces a new section 24 to deal with appeals to the Minister against a decision refusing to classify or reclassify a film on the grounds of national security.

sections.label: Minister deciding national security film appeals
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Minister having authority to decide all appeals regarding films with national security concerns in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In a small, multi-ethnic, multireligious country like Singapore, national security is paramount.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As such, I echo the comments that my colleague, the hon Member Mr Ganesh Rajaram, made and I am supportive of the Minister having the authority to decide all appeals regarding films with national security concerns.

sections.label: Enforcement officers' authority and training
sections.summary: The speaker seeks clarity on the authority section 34A gives IMDA-appointed enforcement officers, their training, and integration with other national security initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While I am supportive of the authority that the Bill gives to the Minister, I would like more clarity on the authority that the amendments in section 34A of the Bill provides IMDA-appointed enforcement officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What training and processes have been put in place to ensure that these officers are equipped with the relevant knowledge to exercise their authority appropriately?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And furthermore, how can we integrate this portion of the Bill with other national security initiatives or measures that MHA or the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) might already have with regard to similar threats to national security from film and media sources?

sections.label: Films up to PG13 co-classification
sections.summary: Minister Yaacob explained co-classification starts with films up to PG13, and IMDA excludes films on race, religion or politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Minister Yaacob had explained this earlier in his opening speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We are starting with films up to PG13 to reduce the impact of any misclassification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: IMDA is also excluding films with content on race, religion or politics from co-classification.

sections.label: Section 33 for PPFs
sections.summary: Section 33 is intended for PPFs which seek to sensationalise or distort serious issues to evoke emotional rather than logical debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Section 33 is intended for PPFs which seek to sensationalise or distort serious issues to evoke emotional, rather than logical debate based on facts.

sections.label: Two films prohibited under ISA
sections.summary: Two films are prohibited for distorted and misleading portrayals of Dr Lim and Said Zahari's 1963 ISA arrest and detention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The two films are prohibited as they gave distorted and misleading portrayals of Dr Lim and Said Zahari's arrest and detention under the ISA in 1963.

sections.label: Industry support for scheme
sections.summary: IMDA has been engaging the industry closely, and distributors and exhibitors have expressed support for the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: IMDA has been engaging the industry closely, and distributors and exhibitors have expressed support for the scheme.

sections.label: Film CA rating limit
sections.summary: Film CAs can only co-classify films up to the PG13 rating.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Second, film CAs can only co-classify films up to the PG13 rating.

sections.label: Co-classification pilot outcomes
sections.summary: Since pilots launched in 2011 and 2015, IMDA has trained and certified 81 film CAs, and almost all co-classified titles match IMDA's ratings.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Since the co-classification pilots were launched with video distributors in 2011 and film exhibitors in 2015, IMDA has trained and certified 81 film CAs, and almost all co-classified titles are in line with IMDA's own ratings.

sections.label: M18 video game sales
sections.summary: Class licence conditions will make clear retailers must ensure M18 video games are not sold to underage consumers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Going forward, the class licence conditions will make clear that retailers must also play their part to protect our minors by ensuring that M18 video games are not sold to underage consumers.

sections.label: Refused Classification term
sections.summary: The new term Refused Classification will more accurately describe IMDA's decision to disallow a film for distribution and public exhibition.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The new term “Refused Classification” will be more accurate in describing IMDA's decision to disallow the film for distribution and public exhibition.

sections.label: Films refused classification material
sections.summary: IMDA will refuse to classify films containing material prescribed, such as content exceeding R21 rating in the guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Kok Heng Leun also asked what the films that might be refused classification under section 16 are, where IMDA will refuse to classify any film that "contains any material prescribed".

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: This refers to existing film content elements that exceed the R21 rating in the film classification guidelines, for instance, gratuitous depictions of extreme cruelty or content that glorifies substance abuse.

sections.label: National security film appeals
sections.summary: IMDA consults security agencies on national security, but agencies may not share full concerns with the FAC, so the Minister should decide appeals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: In determining whether a film is against national security, IMDA will also consult the relevant security agencies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: However, these agencies may face constraints to share the full extent of their security concerns and sensitive information with the FAC, as its members come from non-Government sectors and do not have the necessary security clearances.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: It will be better for the Minister to decide on such appeals as he will be able to consider the appellant’s view, together with IMDA’s considerations and the detailed assessment from security agencies.

sections.label: Minister invoking prohibition section
sections.summary: The Minister exercises judgement on invoking this section, and only two films have been prohibited so far.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The Minister will have to exercise his judgement on whether it is necessary to invoke this section, and I think we have been very judicious, as pointed out by the Senior Minister of State.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: We only have two films so far that have been prohibited.

sections.label: Powers limited to serious offences
sections.summary: Powers are limited to serious offences like prohibited films and unlicensed public exhibition; less serious offences need a Court warrant or owner permission.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: First, we have limited the extension of powers to serious offences, such as those involving prohibited films and the unlicensed public exhibition of films.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: For unlicensed public exhibition, the risk and the ease of flight are high as an exhibition typically lasts two hours or less.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: But for less serious offences, a Court warrant or permission from the owner will be needed for IMDA to exercise these powers.

sections.label: Without-warrant powers conditions
sections.summary: Without-warrant powers are used only when an enforcement officer has reasonable grounds to suspect specified serious offences or evidence that may be concealed, lost or destroyed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Third, Sir, we have specified in the Bill that without-warrant powers will only be used when the enforcement officer has reasonable grounds to suspect that the specified serious offences have been or are being committed, or that evidence of the commission of these offences can be found in the premises and it is necessary to secure it from being concealed, lost or destroyed.

sections.label: Enforcement activities authorised by senior officers
sections.summary: All enforcement activities must be authorised by suitable senior IMDA officers holding the office of a Director or its equivalent.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: First, all enforcement activities have to be authorised by suitable senior IMDA officers holding the office of a Director or its equivalent.

sections.label: Enforcement team leader experience
sections.summary: Team leaders leading enforcement activities have at least five years of enforcement experience.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Team leaders leading enforcement activities have at least five years of enforcement experience.

sections.label: IMDA Internal Audit Unit investigations
sections.summary: Investigations will be conducted by IMDA's Internal Audit Unit, independent of IMDA's regulatory and enforcement divisions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Investigations will be conducted by IMDA's Internal Audit Unit, which is independent of IMDA's regulatory and enforcement divisions.

sections.label: 2009 political films exemption
sections.summary: The FA was amended in 2009 to exempt political films that are factual, objective and not dramatised or distorted.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The FA was then amended in 2009 to exempt and allow political films that are factual and objective and do not dramatise or present a distorted picture.

sections.label: IMDA holistic review of cases
sections.summary: IMDA will look at such cases holistically, considering facts and the intent behind PPF provisions, to keep political discourse sober and rational.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Should cases like the one Mr Kok Heng Leun described arise, IMDA will look at them holistically and consider the facts and circumstances, including the larger intent behind the PPF provisions, to keep our political debates and broader political discourse sober and rational.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Many of the changes in the environment are for the better but there are changes that also pose very real risks for us.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: We are still a city-state with different races and religious groups living closely together on a small, dense island.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: We believe that the amendments are a right step towards finding a course in an increasingly connected and complex media landscape.

sections.label: Minister clarification on co-classification
sections.summary: The speaker takes it that the Minister's clarification is sought on the last point, noting Mr Kok Heng Leun's impression that co-classification stifles creativity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: I will take it that you are seeking the Minister's clarification on your last point.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: I think in his speech, Mr Kok Heng Leun gave the impression that with co-classification, it will stifle creativity.

sections.label: Co-classification and filmmaker creativity
sections.summary: The examples show filmmakers can make a film from R21 down to General, so co-classification will not stifle creativity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The example that I gave and the example that Mr Ganesh Rajaram gave are good examples to demonstrate that filmmakers can actually make a film from R21 all the way downwards to General (G), if they want to do so.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, I do not think this co-classification scheme that we will introduce after the Act is amended will stifle the creativity of filmmakers.

sections.label: Ministerial appeal process
sections.summary: The process adopted will follow all other Ministerial appeal processes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: On the Member's second point, as mentioned in my reply, the process that we will adopt will follow all other Ministerial appeal processes.

sections.label: Streisand effect on banned films
sections.summary: A Member asks whether IMDA looked into the Streisand effect and whether banning two films promoted them instead.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: That is what some of the practitioners would call the Streisand effect.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: So, has IMDA looked into this Streisand effect and see whether the banning of these two films actually helped to encourage and attract more people to go and look for these films and to watch them and, therefore, we have the unintended consequences of actually promoting these films more than prohibiting them?

sections.label: Co-classification sensitive subject matters
sections.summary: Race, religion and politics were mentioned as sensitive subject matters in the context of co-classification, which is not being opened to such films for a start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, I wanted to just put it in context that when we say that race, religion, politics were mentioned as sensitive subject matters, it was in the context of co-classification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We are not opening up this co-classification arrangement to films with content touching on race, religion and politics for a start.

sections.label: Section 35 prohibited films
sections.summary: IMDA and MCI take a judicious and careful approach to section 35 powers on prohibited films, using them as a last resort for egregious content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The second clarification on prohibited films, I think this is why IMDA and MCI, we take a very judicious and careful approach to exercising the powers under section 35 on prohibited films.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Every decision that is taken under section 35, something that we have to go through very careful consideration, and it should be used really as a last resort because there are many other ways – through classification, for example – to be able to deal with some of the risks and concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But we want to keep section 35 provisions to deal with films with egregious content.

sections.label: Film regulation amendments
sections.summary: The Ministry and IMDA are confident the amendments will help film regulations evolve, protect the young, provide adult choices and shape social development.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: My Ministry and IMDA are confident that these amendments will be a positive move to help film regulations in Singapore evolve with the times, protect our young, provide choices for adults and constructively shape our social development as a nation.
